newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Prods - Gasolines end mixed, distilates up.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Prods - Gasolines end mixed, distilates up.

text.p: Gasoline differentials ended mixed Tuesday, while distillate differentials ended mostly stronger.
On NYMEX, August gasoline dipped 0.02 cent to settle on at 60.01 cents a gallon and August heating oil gained 0.35 cent to finish at 52.70 cents a gallon.
MIDCONTINENT
Midcontinent unleaded gasoline differentials were mixed in moderate trade on Tuesday as hype over a fire at a gasoline making unit in a Kansas refinery faded.
The small fire occurred Monday at National Cooperative Refinery Association's 74,000 bpd McPherson facility and reduced gasoline production by an unspecified amount.

Differentials rose on the news Tuesday but eased again in the afternoon as players digested that the cutback would do little to impact already ample supply along the Williams Pipeline, the main system for the Midwest.
In Group Three, prompt unleaded gasoline eased about a quarter cent to put buyers even with August NYMEX futures and sellers at 0.25 cent over the print. Deals even to the screen were done.
Chicago prompt unleaded traded between even to 0.25 cent over the Merc amid some demand. The range is a quarter cent above this morning.
On the distillate side, jet fuel remained strong in Group Three, 1.25/1.50 cents and in Chicago, 2.25/2.50 cents.
U.S. GULF

Regular conventional M1 gasoline differentials eased modestly, with prompt barrels changing hands at 2.95 cents under the August NYMEX, near the bottom of the 2.75 to 3.00 under range created earlier in the day.
"We had a little flourish in here today, but mostly a lot of rolling (of positions)," one Gulf trader said.
Distillate differentials advanced slightly, with players citing a prompt heating oil trade at 2.20 cents under the August NYMEX.
Low sulphur diesel was put at 1.35 cents under the NYMEX, near the top of the trading range made Monday.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Prompt conventional regular M2 gasoline inched higher Tuesday, with players putting barrels between 3.00 and 3.25 cents under the NYMEX, a gain of about 0.25 cent from the previous day.
Reformulated A2 gasoline was talked higher as well, with offers firming to 1.90 cent over the August NYMEX, according to traders.
Low sulphur diesel extended the gains seen Monday, with prompt barrels talked between 1.00 and 1.25 cents over the NYMEX futures.
"When Tosco doesn't sell, that's what happens," one East Coast trader said, referring to maintenance at that company's Bayway, New Jersey refinery on the edge of New York Harbor.
